**2. JUSTIFICATION**

The justification for this change is as follows:

a) **Weather-related service interruptions.** The North-Central region has experienced above-average rainfall since late May 2022. Three of the twelve sites under this contract have suffered weather-related faults during weekend periods when no maintenance crew was on standby. In each case, the fault was not reported until Monday morning, resulting in generation losses of between 18 and 36 hours per incident.

b) **Response time obligations.** Section 9.4 of the contract requires a response time of 24 hours for "urgent faults" that affect grid availability. With the current Monday–Friday schedule, a fault occurring on Saturday cannot be attended within the contractual response window. This creates a compliance risk for GreenGrid Energy PLC with respect to our own offtake agreements.

c) **Rainy season fault patterns.** Historical data from the 2020 and 2021 rainy seasons shows that 62% of all weather-related faults (inverter trips, DC isolator faults, and water ingress in junction boxes) occurred between Friday 17:00 and Monday 08:00. The extension of service hours to include weekends directly addresses this pattern.

d) **Preventive maintenance backlog.** The current preventive maintenance schedule is already at capacity during weekdays. Three routine inspections scheduled for June have been deferred to July due to emergency callouts. Weekend hours will allow the provider to clear this backlog without reducing the responsiveness of the weekday emergency service.

**3. IMPACT ANALYSIS**

**3.1 Impact on Schedule**

The provider's proposed implementation plan indicates that no additional mobilisation time is required. The existing crew rotation can accommodate weekend coverage by reallocating the current weekday rosters. The provider has indicated that this change will not delay any existing preventive maintenance milestones under the 2022 Maintenance Plan (Appendix C of the contract).

**3.2 Impact on Cost**

The provider has noted that this estimate is provisional and subject to revision following the submission of a detailed breakdown, which is expected within five working days of this request.

**3.3 Impact on Contract Terms**

This change request does not alter any other terms of the contract, including but not limited to: service level agreements, response times, reporting obligations, or the scope of maintenance services. The extension of maintenance hours applies solely to the service hours clause and does not constitute a change to the definition of "Maintenance Services" in Section 1.1 of the contract.

Mrs. Adeyemi opened the session by confirming that the Client had received the Contractor’s submission dated 28 May 2022 regarding the proposed installation of an automated cleaning system for the Kainji North Field solar array. She noted that the original scope of the Framework Agreement (Clause 4.2) did not include automated cleaning equipment, and that the current manual cleaning regime had been identified as a recurring bottleneck during the harmattan season.

Engr. Okafor presented the technical basis for the request. He explained that the existing manual cleaning crew of twelve personnel could only cover approximately 15% of the North Field panels per day, leading to a cumulative soiling loss of up to 8% of expected yield during the December–February period. He referenced the performance data from the 2021/2022 harmattan season, which showed a 6.2% shortfall against the agreed availability target of 98.5%. The proposed automated system would consist of two robotic cleaning units operating along the existing tracker rows, with a water recirculation unit and a control cabinet.

Mr. Eze asked about the compatibility of the robotic units with the existing trackers, which were manufactured by a different supplier. Mr. Bakare confirmed that the Contractor had conducted a site survey in April 2022 and had obtained the tracker manufacturer’s written confirmation that the rail profile was compatible. He presented the manufacturer’s letter, which was accepted as evidence.

- Control cabinet, sensors, and cabling: NGN 5,150,000

The backup pump may be added later under a separate change request if operational experience justifies it.

The revised total was therefore confirmed at NGN 47,300,000 (excluding VAT). The Chair asked both parties to confirm that no further cost adjustments were outstanding. Both parties confirmed.

documents.content:
**2. JUSTIFICATION**

The justification for this change is as follows:

a) **Weather-related service interruptions.** The North-Central region has experienced above-average rainfall since late May 2022. Three of the twelve sites under this contract have suffered weather-related faults during weekend periods when no maintenance crew was on standby. In each case, the fault was not reported until Monday morning, resulting in generation losses of between 18 and 36 hours per incident.

b) **Response time obligations.** Section 9.4 of the contract requires a response time of 24 hours for "urgent faults" that affect grid availability. With the current Monday–Friday schedule, a fault occurring on Saturday cannot be attended within the contractual response window. This creates a compliance risk for GreenGrid Energy PLC with respect to our own offtake agreements.

c) **Rainy season fault patterns.** Historical data from the 2020 and 2021 rainy seasons shows that 62% of all weather-related faults (inverter trips, DC isolator faults, and water ingress in junction boxes) occurred between Friday 17:00 and Monday 08:00. The extension of service hours to include weekends directly addresses this pattern.

d) **Preventive maintenance backlog.** The current preventive maintenance schedule is already at capacity during weekdays. Three routine inspections scheduled for June have been deferred to July due to emergency callouts. Weekend hours will allow the provider to clear this backlog without reducing the responsiveness of the weekday emergency service.

**3. IMPACT ANALYSIS**

**3.1 Impact on Schedule**

The provider's proposed implementation plan indicates that no additional mobilisation time is required. The existing crew rotation can accommodate weekend coverage by reallocating the current weekday rosters. The provider has indicated that this change will not delay any existing preventive maintenance milestones under the 2022 Maintenance Plan (Appendix C of the contract).

**3.2 Impact on Cost**

Change Request CR-2022-014 requested_change is to extend maintenance hours to include weekends during rainy season. Record status: current.

The provider has submitted a preliminary cost impact estimate of NGN 1,240,000 (one million, two hundred and forty thousand Naira) per month for the five-month duration of the rainy season extension (July–November 2022), excluding VAT. This estimate is based on:

- Additional crew allowances for weekend work: NGN 720,000/month
- Additional transport and logistics (weekend fuel, driver allowances): NGN 310,000/month
- Additional site security coordination: NGN 210,000/month

The total estimated cost impact for the 2022 rainy season is NGN 6,200,000 (six million, two hundred thousand Naira) excluding VAT. The provider has noted that this estimate is provisional and subject to revision following the submission of a detailed breakdown, which is expected within five working days of this request.

**3.3 Impact on Contract Terms**

This change request does not alter any other terms of the contract, including but not limited to: service level agreements, response times, reporting obligations, or the scope of maintenance services. The extension of maintenance hours applies solely to the service hours clause and does not constitute a change to the definition of "Maintenance Services" in Section 1.1 of the contract.

**4. PROPOSED IMPLEMENTATION**

Subject to agreement on the cost impact, the implementation of this change will proceed as follows:

- Week 1 (w/c 20 June 2022): Provider to revise crew rosters and confirm weekend availability for all twelve sites.
- Week 2 (w/c 27 June 2022): Provider to brief all maintenance technicians on revised hours; GreenGrid to update the site access register for weekend entries.
- 1 July 2022: Commencement of weekend maintenance hours.
- 30 November 2022: End of weekend maintenance hours; service hours revert to the standard schedule.

**5. COMMERCIAL TERMS AND NEGOTIATION NOTES**

The following notes are recorded for the attention of the contract negotiation team. These are preliminary positions and do not constitute a formal agreement.

DISCUSSION SUMMARY

Item 1 – Review of Change Request CR-2022-014
Mrs. Adeyemi opened the session by confirming that the Client had received the Contractor’s submission dated 28 May 2022 regarding the proposed installation of an automated cleaning system for the Kainji North Field solar array. She noted that the original scope of the Framework Agreement (Clause 4.2) did not include automated cleaning equipment, and that the current manual cleaning regime had been identified as a recurring bottleneck during the harmattan season.

Engr. Okafor presented the technical basis for the request. He explained that the existing manual cleaning crew of twelve personnel could only cover approximately 15% of the North Field panels per day, leading to a cumulative soiling loss of up to 8% of expected yield during the December–February period. He referenced the performance data from the 2021/2022 harmattan season, which showed a 6.2% shortfall against the agreed availability target of 98.5%. The proposed automated system would consist of two robotic cleaning units operating along the existing tracker rows, with a water recirculation unit and a control cabinet.

Mr. Eze asked about the compatibility of the robotic units with the existing trackers, which were manufactured by a different supplier. Mr. Bakare confirmed that the Contractor had conducted a site survey in April 2022 and had obtained the tracker manufacturer’s written confirmation that the rail profile was compatible. He presented the manufacturer’s letter, which was accepted as evidence.

Item 2 – Technical assessment and cost implications
The Contractor’s detailed cost breakdown was tabled. The total estimated cost of the change was NGN 48,750,000, broken down as follows:
- Two robotic cleaning units: NGN 27,400,000
- Water recirculation unit and piping: NGN 6,800,000
- Control cabinet, sensors, and cabling: NGN 5,150,000
- Installation labour (including scaffolding and crane hire): NGN 4,600,000
- Training of two operators (one week, on-site): NGN 1,200,000
- Spare parts and consumables (first year): NGN 2,100,000
- Contingency (5%): NGN 1,500,000

Change Request CR-2022-014 approval_status is approved with cost adjustment. Record status: current.

Mr. Danjuma noted that the Client’s budget review had flagged the contingency as excessive, given that the Contractor had already completed a similar installation at the Jebba South field in 2020. He also questioned the inclusion of a full set of spare parts for the first year, suggesting that the warranty should cover certain components.

Engr. Okafor responded that the Jebba installation had been a smaller system (one unit) and that the Kainji North field had a higher dust load due to its proximity to the access road. He agreed, however, to reduce the contingency from 5% to 3%, bringing the total to NGN 48,300,000. He also noted that the spare parts list could be trimmed by excluding the drive belts, which were covered under the manufacturer’s 24-month warranty.

Item 3 – Schedule impact and resource availability
Mr. Bakare outlined the proposed implementation schedule:
- Mobilisation and delivery of equipment: 4 weeks from approval
- Civil works (concrete pads for the control cabinet and water unit): 2 weeks
- Installation and cabling: 3 weeks
- Commissioning and operator training: 1 week
- Total duration: 10 weeks

He noted that the installation could be carried out without shutting down the array, as the robotic units operate on a separate rail and the control cabinet would be installed on the non-energised side of the inverter shelter. The only planned outage would be a two-hour window for the final connection to the low-voltage distribution board, which would be scheduled during a maintenance window already agreed for July 2022.

Mrs. Adeyemi asked whether the Contractor had considered the rainy season impact on the installation works. Mr. Bakare confirmed that the civil works would be completed by mid-August, before the peak rainfall period, and that the cabling would be installed in conduit with IP67-rated junction boxes.
